items.project_definition: Restrictive database rules, specifically the composite unique requirement preventing duplicate entries for the same pair of associated identifiers.

An example of a short-form identification string for a specific athletic club.
The set of business rules ensuring logical consistency for sporting events, such as forbidding a team from playing against itself and requiring final scores upon completion.
The structural links between different data entities, including one-to-many and many-to-many associations.
Operational checks verifying that no two athletic organizations share the same identity name.
The standardized global time reference used to avoid ambiguity across different geographical time zones.
A 128-bit universally unique identifier used as the primary key for all major system entities.
The integrity checks performed on account data, focusing on the uniqueness of contact addresses and credential strength.
A junction entity tracking the subscription interest of a profile toward a specific sporting event.
